name: Crack-reporting concrete
subtitle: concrete that seals and shows its repairs

effects.effect: heating limestone frees a gas that lime soaks back up
a jellyfish protein makes any cell that carries its gene glow green
a cell can run on a genome written entirely by computer

effect: heating limestone frees a gas that lime soaks back up
how: Bridges and tunnels are inspected by eye, which finds the cracks that show and misses the ones inside where water is already rusting the steel. Spores mixed into concrete wake when a crack lets in water and lay down limestone that seals it, a trick already used in a few buildings. Giving those organisms a glowing protein as well makes every repair site visible under a blue lamp, so an inspector walking the structure reads a map of where it has been working hardest.
obstacle: The spores have to survive years in the dry alkaline concrete and still glow brightly enough to see through a wet crack.
why: Healing concrete is sold; a built-in visual record of repairs is new.
real: Bacterial self-healing concrete that seals cracks by microbial calcite precipitation is real and commercially demonstrated, but no fluorescent or GFP-tagged reporting of repair sites was found; healing is still assessed visually, microscopically or ultrasonically.
